query: East Marginal Way South & 1st Avenue South

junction.name: East Marginal Way South & 1st Avenue South, Seattle

claims.text: East Marginal Way South & 1st Avenue South had 51 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 1 person killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $3.5 million a year.
34% of crashes here happened on a wet or icy road, against 19% at the city's worst crash locations.
18% of crashes here were recorded as “sideswipe” crashes, against 10% at the city's worst crash locations.
15% of crashes here were recorded as “fixed object” crashes, against 6% at the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.
Pavement Friction Management would avoid about 2.0 crashes a year (CMF 195, the only eligible record; evidence: national studies only), worth $671,000 a year.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 1.5 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $524,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for 1st Avenue South (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
The state transportation department (route designation only; confirm ownership) is responsible for East Marginal Way South (signed route in OpenStreetMap; owner not confirmed).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) and the state transportation department (route designation only; confirm ownership) is ready to draft from these facts.
